optionExplanations.2: C2H4 has a double bond and three sigma domains per carbon, giving sp2.
optionExplanations.3: CH3OH carbons have four single bonds, giving sp3 hybridization.

formulaNotes: sp: 2 domains; sp2: 3 domains; sp3: 4 domains

shortExplanation: Unlike the ideal gas model, real gas particles do experience intermolecular attractions, causing deviations from ideal behavior.
solutionSteps: The ideal gas model assumes no intermolecular forces and negligible particle volume.
Real gases have measurable intermolecular attractions and finite molecular volume.
The key contrast is that real gas particles experience intermolecular forces.
keyConcept: Real gases deviate from ideal behavior due to intermolecular forces and finite molecular volume.
commonMistake: Reversing the assumptions and stating that ideal (not real) particles feel intermolecular forces.

optionExplanations.0: It is ideal gas particles that are assumed to have negligible volume, not real ones.
optionExplanations.2: Both models treat collisions as elastic; that is not the distinguishing feature.
optionExplanations.3: Real gas pressure is not always higher; attractions often make it lower than ideal.

shortExplanation: Molar mass equals density times molar volume at STP: 1.96 g/L * 22.4 L/mol = 43.9 g/mol, about 44.0 g/mol.
solutionSteps: At STP, molar mass M = density * molar volume.
M = 43.9 g/mol, which rounds to 44.0 g/mol.
keyConcept: M = density * molar volume for a gas at STP.
commonMistake: Dividing density by molar volume instead of multiplying.

optionExplanations.1: 32.0 g/mol would require a density of about 1.43 g/L.
optionExplanations.2: 39.2 g/mol comes from a mis-multiplication (e.g., 1.96 * 20).
optionExplanations.3: 22.4 g/mol wrongly uses the molar volume as the mass.

shortExplanation: HF molecules link to each other through hydrogen bonds because F is small and highly electronegative, and breaking this extra network of bonds requires much more energy than for HCl, so the boiling point is raised.
solutionSteps: Hydrogen bonding occurs when H is bonded to N, O, or F.
In HF, H is bonded directly to F, so HF molecules hydrogen-bond to one another.
Cl is larger and less electronegative, so HCl shows only ordinary dipole-dipole forces, not true hydrogen bonds.
Extra energy is needed to break the HF hydrogen-bond network, raising its boiling point above HCl.
keyConcept: Hydrogen bonding (H to F) is a much stronger intermolecular force than the dipole-dipole attraction in HCl.
commonMistake: Confusing acid strength (HF is actually the weaker acid) with boiling point, which is set by intermolecular forces.

optionExplanations.0: Acid strength in water does not determine boiling point, and HF is in fact the weaker acid.
optionExplanations.1: Fluorine is more electronegative than chlorine, not less, so this statement is factually wrong.
optionExplanations.2: Both molecules have dipole-dipole interactions; ordinary dipole-dipole forces alone cannot explain the large gap, only hydrogen bonding does.

shortExplanation: Dividing each mass percent by the atomic mass gives moles in a 1:2:1 ratio for C:H:O, so the empirical formula is CH2O.
solutionSteps: Assume 100 g: 40.0 g C, 6.7 g H, 53.3 g O.
Divide by the smallest (3.33): C = 1, H = 2, O = 1.
Empirical formula = CH2O.
keyConcept: Empirical formula comes from the smallest whole-number mole ratio of the elements.
commonMistake: Reporting a molecular formula such as C2H4O2 when only mass percent (not molar mass) is given, which fixes only the empirical ratio.

optionExplanations.0: CHO gives a 1:1:1 ratio, but H is present in double the moles of C and O.
optionExplanations.2: C2H4O2 has the correct ratio but is a multiple; without a molar mass the answer must be the simplest ratio.
optionExplanations.3: C3H6O has ratio 3:6:1, which does not match the equal C and O mole amounts.

formulaNotes: moles = mass / atomic mass; empirical formula = simplest whole-number mole ratio.

shortExplanation: XeF4 has 4 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs on Xe; the two lone pairs sit opposite each other, leaving the four F atoms in a square planar arrangement.
solutionSteps: Xe has 8 valence electrons; four bond to F, leaving 2 lone pairs.
Total electron domains = 6, giving an octahedral electron geometry.
The two lone pairs occupy opposite (axial) positions to minimize repulsion.
The remaining four F atoms lie in one plane, so the molecular shape is square planar.
keyConcept: AX4E2 electron arrangement (octahedral) with two axial lone pairs gives square planar molecular geometry.
commonMistake: Ignoring the two lone pairs and calling it tetrahedral, or placing lone pairs incorrectly to get square pyramidal.

optionExplanations.0: Tetrahedral would require 4 domains only; XeF4 has 6 domains including two lone pairs.
optionExplanations.1: Square pyramidal (AX5E) has one lone pair; XeF4 has two lone pairs.
optionExplanations.3: See-saw (AX4E) has one lone pair and a trigonal-bipyramidal base, not two lone pairs in an octahedron.

shortExplanation: Sublimation (solid to gas) requires the system to absorb energy to overcome intermolecular forces, making it endothermic.
solutionSteps: Endothermic changes absorb heat and move toward a more disordered, higher-energy state.
Freezing, condensation, and deposition all release heat (exothermic).
Sublimation goes from solid directly to gas, requiring absorbed energy, so it is endothermic.
keyConcept: Melting, vaporization, and sublimation absorb energy (endothermic); freezing, condensation, and deposition release energy (exothermic).
commonMistake: Mixing up sublimation (solid to gas, endothermic) with deposition (gas to solid, exothermic).

optionExplanations.0: Freezing (liquid to solid) releases heat, so it is exothermic.
optionExplanations.1: Condensation (gas to liquid) releases heat, so it is exothermic.
optionExplanations.3: Deposition (gas to solid) releases heat, so it is exothermic.

shortExplanation: Chromium is an exception to the normal filling order: one 4s electron moves to 3d to give a stable half-filled d subshell, giving [Ar]4s1 3d5.
solutionSteps: Expected filling would give [Ar]4s2 3d4.
A half-filled 3d5 configuration is extra stable due to exchange energy and symmetry.
One 4s electron is promoted to 3d, giving [Ar]4s1 3d5.
This accounts for all 24 electrons of chromium.
keyConcept: Cr and Cu are anomalies: they promote a 4s electron to achieve a half-filled or fully filled d subshell.
commonMistake: Applying the strict Aufbau order and writing [Ar]4s2 3d4 instead of the more stable half-filled form.

optionExplanations.0: [Ar]4s2 3d4 is the naive Aufbau result but is less stable than the half-filled configuration.
optionExplanations.2: [Ar]4s0 3d6 gives the wrong electron count distribution and is not the ground state of neutral Cr.
optionExplanations.3: [Ar]4s2 4p4 skips the 3d subshell entirely, which must fill before 4p.

shortExplanation: Glucose molar mass is 180 g/mol; oxygen contributes 6 x 16 = 96 g. Mass percent = 96/180 = 53.3%.
solutionSteps: Mass of oxygen = 6 x 16 = 96 g.
Mass percent O = 96 / 180 x 100.
keyConcept: Mass percent of an element = (element's total mass / molar mass) x 100.
commonMistake: Using the count of atoms (6/24 = 25%) instead of their mass contributions.

optionExplanations.0: 40.0% understates oxygen's mass share.
optionExplanations.2: 60.0% overstates oxygen's mass share.
optionExplanations.3: 46.7% is the combined carbon-plus-hydrogen fraction, not oxygen's.

shortExplanation: In an exothermic reaction, more energy is released forming product bonds than is absorbed breaking reactant bonds, so the product bonds are stronger (higher total bond energy).
solutionSteps: ΔH is approximately (bonds broken) minus (bonds formed) in energy terms.
Exothermic (ΔH < 0) means the energy released forming products exceeds the energy needed to break reactants.
Therefore product bonds are stronger, i.e. product bond energy is higher than reactant bond energy.
keyConcept: Exothermic reactions form stronger (more stable, higher-energy-release) bonds in the products.
commonMistake: Confusing 'higher bond energy' (stronger bonds, more stable) with 'higher potential energy' of the molecules.

optionExplanations.0: If reactant bonds were stronger, breaking them would cost more than forming products, giving an endothermic reaction.
optionExplanations.2: Equal bond energies would give ΔH near zero; activation energy does not determine ΔH.
optionExplanations.3: ΔH is directly related to the difference in bond energies, not independent of them.

formulaNotes: ΔH ≈ (sum of bond energies broken) - (sum of bond energies formed)

shortExplanation: Each half-life halves the concentration: 0.8 -> 0.4 -> 0.2 -> 0.1 takes 3 half-lives = 3 x 20 = 60 minutes.
solutionSteps: After one half-life (20 min): 0.8 -> 0.4 M.
After two half-lives (40 min): 0.4 -> 0.2 M.
After three half-lives (60 min): 0.2 -> 0.1 M.
Total time = 60 minutes.
keyConcept: For first-order kinetics, each half-life reduces the concentration by half regardless of starting amount.
commonMistake: Assuming linear decay and stopping after two half-lives (40 min) instead of three.

optionExplanations.0: 40 minutes is only two half-lives, reaching 0.2 M, not 0.1 M.
optionExplanations.2: 80 minutes is four half-lives, overshooting to 0.05 M.
optionExplanations.3: 100 minutes is five half-lives, far below 0.1 M.

shortExplanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy for both directions equally, speeding forward and reverse reactions the same, so equilibrium is reached faster but its position is unchanged.
solutionSteps: A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy.
This accelerates the forward and reverse reactions by the same factor.
The equilibrium position (K) is unchanged; only the time to reach it decreases.
keyConcept: Catalysts speed both directions equally and do not shift equilibrium position.
commonMistake: Believing a catalyst shifts equilibrium toward products; it only shortens the time to reach the same equilibrium.

optionExplanations.0: A catalyst does not shift equilibrium toward products.
optionExplanations.1: A catalyst does not shift equilibrium toward reactants.
optionExplanations.2: A catalyst lowers, not increases, the activation energy.

shortExplanation: A negative ΔG means the reaction is spontaneous, and negative ΔG defines an exergonic process.
solutionSteps: Spontaneity is determined by the sign of ΔG.
ΔG < 0 means the reaction proceeds spontaneously.
A reaction with negative ΔG is, by definition, exergonic.
keyConcept: ΔG < 0 indicates a spontaneous, exergonic reaction.
commonMistake: Confusing exergonic/endergonic (about ΔG, free energy) with exothermic/endothermic (about ΔH, heat).

optionExplanations.0: Negative ΔG means spontaneous, not non-spontaneous; ΔG does not directly give ΔH.
optionExplanations.1: Spontaneous is correct, but negative ΔG is exergonic, not endergonic.
optionExplanations.3: At equilibrium ΔG = 0, not -150 kJ/mol.

shortExplanation: Moles of NaCl = 58.5 g / 58.5 g/mol = 1 mol in 1 L, giving 1.0 M.
solutionSteps: Moles = mass / molar mass = 58.5 / 58.5 = 1 mol.
Molarity = moles / volume in liters = 1 / 1.
keyConcept: Molarity = moles of solute per liter of solution.
commonMistake: Dividing mass directly by volume without converting to moles.

optionExplanations.0: 0.5 M would require only 0.5 mol (29.25 g).
optionExplanations.2: 1.5 M would require 1.5 mol (87.75 g).
optionExplanations.3: 2.0 M would require 2 mol (117 g).

shortExplanation: Boyle's Law states that at constant temperature, gas pressure is inversely proportional to volume (P x V = constant).
solutionSteps: Identify the variables held constant: temperature and amount of gas.
Boyle's Law: P is inversely proportional to V at constant T.
So P x V = constant.
keyConcept: Boyle's Law: P and V are inversely related at constant temperature.
commonMistake: Confusing Boyle's Law with Charles' Law, which relates volume and temperature.

optionExplanations.1: Charles' Law relates volume directly to temperature at constant pressure.
optionExplanations.2: Gay-Lussac's Law relates pressure directly to temperature at constant volume.
optionExplanations.3: Avogadro's Law relates volume to the amount (moles) of gas.

formulaNotes: Boyle: P x V = constant (constant T)

shortExplanation: Elements in the periodic table are arranged in order of increasing atomic number, i.e. the number of protons in the nucleus.
solutionSteps: The defining property of an element is its atomic number Z = number of protons.
Moseley established that ordering by atomic number resolves periodic-law anomalies.
Reading left to right and top to bottom, Z increases by one at each element.
Hence the ordering criterion is the number of protons.
keyConcept: Atomic number (proton count) is the fundamental ordering principle of the periodic table.
commonMistake: Thinking elements are ordered by atomic mass; mass ordering fails for a few pairs (e.g. Ar/K).

optionExplanations.1: Alphabetical order would scatter chemically similar elements across the table.
optionExplanations.2: Cosmic abundance does not determine periodic-table position.
optionExplanations.4: Discovery date has no relation to an element's position in the table.

shortExplanation: The claim is false, and a counterexample needs a number whose digit sum is divisible by 6 while the number itself is not. 3333 has digit sum 12 (divisible by 6) but is odd, so it is not divisible by 6.
solutionSteps: Divisibility by 6 requires divisibility by both 2 and 3.
A digit sum divisible by 6 guarantees divisibility by 3 but says nothing about divisibility by 2.
For 3333 the digit sum is 3+3+3+3 = 12, which is divisible by 6.
But 3333 is odd, so it is not divisible by 2 and hence not by 6.
The rule 'divisible by 6 iff digit sum divisible by 6' therefore fails here.
keyConcept: Divisibility by 6 = divisibility by 2 AND by 3; the digit-sum test only controls the factor 3.
commonMistake: Assuming a digit-sum criterion works for 6 the same way it does for 3 or 9.

optionExplanations.1: 6666 has digit sum 24 (divisible by 6) and equals 6*1111, so it IS divisible by 6 — the rule holds, no contradiction.
optionExplanations.2: 5505 has digit sum 15 (not divisible by 6) and 5505 is not divisible by 6, so both sides of the biconditional are false — consistent, not a counterexample.
optionExplanations.4: 4404 has digit sum 12 (divisible by 6) and equals 6*734, so it is divisible by 6 — the rule holds.

formulaNotes: n divisible by 6 <=> n even AND digit-sum divisible by 3.

shortExplanation: Since 2^4 = 16 and 2^5 = 32, and 16 < 18 < 32, the exponent log2(18) lies strictly between 4 and 5.
solutionSteps: log2(18) is the power to which 2 must be raised to give 18.
Compute 2^4 = 16 and 2^5 = 32.
Because 16 < 18 < 32, the exponent satisfies 4 < log2(18) < 5.
keyConcept: Bracket a logarithm by finding the two consecutive integer powers of the base that straddle the argument.
commonMistake: Confusing log2(18) with a value near 9 by mistaking the logarithm for a simple division 18/2.

optionExplanations.1: 'less than 4' fails because 2^4 = 16 is already below 18, so the exponent exceeds 4.
optionExplanations.2: 'equal to 9' would mean 2^9 = 512, far larger than 18.
optionExplanations.3: 'greater than 5' would require 18 > 32, which is false.

shortExplanation: Three exams averaging 24 give a total of 72; adding 30 gives 102 over four exams, i.e. an average of 25.5/30.
solutionSteps: Total of first three exams = 3 * 24 = 72.
Add the fourth score: 72 + 30 = 102.
Divide by the number of exams: 102 / 4 = 25.5.
keyConcept: Average = sum of scores divided by the number of scores; recover the sum before recomputing.
commonMistake: Averaging 24 and 30 as if only two numbers mattered, ignoring that the 24 already represents three exams.

optionExplanations.1: 'Data not enough' is wrong because the running average and count fully determine the total.
optionExplanations.2: 26.5 would require a total of 106, but the total is 102.
optionExplanations.3: 27 would require a total of 108, again too high.

shortExplanation: Both logarithms require positive arguments, forcing x > 1; there the base-10 log is increasing so log(x) > log(x-1) holds automatically. The solution is x > 1.
solutionSteps: Domain: need x > 0 and x - 1 > 0, so x > 1.
log10 is strictly increasing, so log(x) > log(x-1) is equivalent to x > x - 1.
x > x - 1 is always true, so the inequality holds throughout the domain.
Solution set: x > 1.
keyConcept: Always intersect the solution with the logarithm's domain (arguments must be positive).
commonMistake: Forgetting the domain constraint x - 1 > 0 and reporting all x > 0.

optionExplanations.1: '0 < x < 1' violates x - 1 > 0, so log(x-1) is undefined there.
optionExplanations.2: 'x > 0' includes 0 < x <= 1 where the right-hand logarithm is undefined.
optionExplanations.3: 'every real value' ignores that negative and small arguments make the logarithms undefined.

formulaNotes: For increasing f, f(u) > f(v) <=> u > v, valid only on the common domain.

shortExplanation: The set of points equidistant from two fixed distinct points is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them, which is a single straight line.
solutionSteps: Let the two fixed points be A and B.
A point P is equidistant when PA = PB.
This condition defines the perpendicular bisector of segment AB.
The perpendicular bisector is one straight line.
keyConcept: Equidistance from two points <=> lying on the perpendicular bisector, always a single line.
commonMistake: Thinking two-point equidistance produces a curve like an ellipse (that comes from a sum of distances, not equality).

optionExplanations.0: 'one or two lines depending on position' is wrong; the answer is always exactly one line for distinct points.
optionExplanations.2: An ellipse is the locus of constant SUM of distances to two foci, not equal distances.
optionExplanations.4: Two perpendicular lines would come from equating distances to two lines, not two points.

shortExplanation: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, so with side s and one diagonal equal to s, the half-diagonals satisfy (s/2)^2 + (d/2)^2 = s^2, giving the other diagonal d = s*sqrt(3).
solutionSteps: Let side = s and let one diagonal equal s.
Diagonals meet at right angles and bisect each other, forming a right triangle with legs s/2 and d/2 and hypotenuse s.
d/2 = s*sqrt(3)/2, so d = s*sqrt(3).
keyConcept: In a rhombus the diagonals are perpendicular bisectors, so half-diagonals and the side form a right triangle.
commonMistake: Assuming the two diagonals are equal (that only holds for a square).

optionExplanations.1: 'equal to the side' would make all half-triangle legs equal, contradicting the Pythagorean relation.
optionExplanations.3: sqrt(2) times the side comes from a square's diagonal, not this configuration.
optionExplanations.4: Double the side is impossible since a diagonal is shorter than twice the side by the triangle inequality here.

formulaNotes: (d1/2)^2 + (d2/2)^2 = s^2 for a rhombus of side s.

shortExplanation: 3 radians is about 171.9 degrees, placing the angle in the second quadrant where cosine is negative. Hence cos(alpha) < 0.
solutionSteps: Since pi/2 ≈ 1.571 < 3 < pi ≈ 3.1416, the angle is in the second quadrant.
In the second quadrant sine is positive but cosine and tangent are negative.
Therefore cos(alpha) < 0 is the true statement.
keyConcept: Locate the quadrant from the radian value, then read off the signs of the trig functions.
commonMistake: Forgetting that 3 radians is nearly 172 degrees, not a small first-quadrant angle.

optionExplanations.0: tan(alpha) > 0 is false; in the second quadrant tangent is negative.
optionExplanations.4: cos(3) ≈ -0.99, nowhere near 1/10.

shortExplanation: With sides 5k and 2k, the area 10k^2 = 90 gives k = 3, so sides are 15 and 6 and the perimeter is 2(15+6) = 42 cm.
solutionSteps: Let sides be 5k and 2k.
Area = 5k * 2k = 10k^2 = 90, so k^2 = 9 and k = 3.
Sides are 15 cm and 6 cm.
Perimeter = 2(15 + 6) = 42 cm.
keyConcept: Introduce a common factor k for a given ratio, solve using the area, then compute the perimeter.
commonMistake: Adding the raw ratio numbers 5 and 2 without scaling by the area-derived factor.

optionExplanations.1: 38 cm does not match sides 15 and 6.
optionExplanations.3: 21 cm is just the semiperimeter, not the full perimeter.
optionExplanations.4: 14 cm ignores the correct side lengths entirely.

shortExplanation: A parabola with axis parallel to the x-axis has the form x = a*y^2 + ..., i.e. y is squared and x appears linearly. The equation y^2 = x + 2 fits this, opening along the x-axis.
solutionSteps: A parabola with axis parallel to the x-axis is written x as a quadratic in y (y is the squared variable).
Rewrite y^2 = x + 2 as x = y^2 - 2, a parabola opening in the x-direction.
Its axis is the horizontal line y = 0, parallel to the x-axis.
keyConcept: Axis parallel to x-axis => y is squared and x is linear (x = ay^2 + by + c).
commonMistake: Choosing y = 2x^2, which is a parabola with axis parallel to the y-axis instead.

optionExplanations.0: y = 2x^2 is a parabola but its axis is parallel to the y-axis.
optionExplanations.1: y = 3x - 1 is a straight line, not a parabola.
optionExplanations.2: x^2 + 2xy + y^2 - x = 1 factors around (x+y)^2, a degenerate/rotated conic, not this parabola.

formulaNotes: x = a*y^2 + b*y + c has a horizontal axis of symmetry.

shortExplanation: Vanishing at x = 2 and x = -2 means the polynomial is divisible by (x-2)(x+2) = x^2 - 4. Testing shows P(x) = 2x^3 + x^2 - 8x - 4 gives P(2) = 0 and P(-2) = 0.
solutionSteps: A polynomial vanishing at 2 and -2 must be divisible by (x-2)(x+2) = x^2 - 4.
For 2x^3 + x^2 - 8x - 4, factor by grouping: x^2(2x+1) - 4(2x+1) = (2x+1)(x^2-4).
So the roots are x = -1/2, x = 2, x = -2.
keyConcept: Given roots, factor out the corresponding linear (or product) factors and verify by substitution.
commonMistake: Only checking one of the two required roots and stopping too early.
formulaNotes: If a and b are roots, the polynomial is divisible by (x-a)(x-b).

shortExplanation: Both P(1,1) and Q(3,3) satisfy y = x (equal coordinates), and the slope through them is (3-1)/(3-1) = 1 through the origin, giving y = x.
solutionSteps: Using point (1,1): y - 1 = 1*(x - 1) => y = x.
Check (3,3): 3 = 3, satisfied.
keyConcept: Line through two points: compute the slope, then apply point-slope form.
commonMistake: Reading the slope as 3 from the coordinate 3 rather than computing rise over run.

optionExplanations.0: x = 1 is a vertical line through P but misses Q(3,3).
optionExplanations.1: y = 3x passes through the origin with slope 3, giving y = 3 at x = 1, not 1.
optionExplanations.2: y = 3 is horizontal and does not pass through (1,1).

shortExplanation: Numerically pi/2 ≈ 1.571, 2/pi ≈ 0.637, 2/pi^2 ≈ 0.203, 3/5 = 0.6, so the ascending order is 2/pi^2 < 3/5 < 2/pi < pi/2.
keyConcept: Convert symbolic expressions to decimal approximations to compare and order them.
commonMistake: Confusing 2/pi (about 0.637) with 3/5 (0.6), which are close and easy to swap.

optionExplanations.2: '2/pi^2 < 3/5 < pi/2 < 2/pi' wrongly ranks pi/2 (1.571) below 2/pi (0.637).
optionExplanations.4: '2/pi < pi/2 < 3/5 < 2/pi^2' scrambles nearly every value.

shortExplanation: The distance between centers (3 cm) equals the difference of the radii (5 - 2 = 3 cm), so the circles touch at exactly one point with the smaller inside the larger: internally tangent.
solutionSteps: Let d = 3 (center distance), R = 5, r = 2.
Compute R - r = 3 and R + r = 7.
Since d = R - r = 3, the circles are internally tangent (one point of contact).
The smaller circle lies inside the larger, touching it once.
keyConcept: Compare center distance d with R+r and |R-r|: d = |R-r| means internal tangency.
commonMistake: Confusing internal tangency (d = R - r) with external tangency (d = R + r).

optionExplanations.0: External tangency needs d = R + r = 7, but d = 3.
optionExplanations.1: Two intersection points require |R-r| < d < R+r, i.e. 3 < d < 7, but d = 3 exactly.
optionExplanations.3: 'internal, no contact' requires d < R - r = 3, but d equals 3.

formulaNotes: Internally tangent when d = |R - r|; externally tangent when d = R + r.

shortExplanation: The 5 cm cathetus is adjacent to the given angle, so cos = adjacent/hypotenuse = 5/hyp = 4/5, giving hypotenuse = 25/4 = 6.25 cm.
solutionSteps: For the given angle, cosine = (adjacent cathetus)/(hypotenuse).
The adjacent cathetus is 5, so 5/hyp = 4/5.
keyConcept: In a right triangle, cos(angle) = adjacent leg / hypotenuse.
commonMistake: Multiplying 5 by 4/5 (getting 4) instead of dividing, which confuses adjacent leg with hypotenuse.

optionExplanations.1: 3 would be the opposite leg (via sin = 3/5), not the hypotenuse.
optionExplanations.2: 4 comes from computing 5 * 4/5, incorrectly treating the hypotenuse as the leg.
optionExplanations.3: 10 doubles the answer with no basis in the ratio.

shortExplanation: Multiply degrees by pi/180: 15 * pi/180 = pi/12 radians.
solutionSteps: Conversion factor: radians = degrees * pi/180.
Simplify 15/180 = 1/12, so the measure is pi/12.
keyConcept: Degrees to radians: multiply by pi/180.
commonMistake: Simplifying 15/180 incorrectly (e.g. to 1/24) and getting pi/24.

optionExplanations.1: pi/24 would correspond to 7.5 degrees.
optionExplanations.2: pi/2 corresponds to 90 degrees.
optionExplanations.3: pi/18 corresponds to 10 degrees.

shortExplanation: In the right triangle ABH (with H the foot of the altitude on BC), sin(beta) = AH/AB, so the altitude AH = AB * sin(beta).
solutionSteps: H is the foot of the perpendicular from A to BC, so triangle ABH is right-angled at H.
In triangle ABH the angle at B is beta and AB is the hypotenuse.
sin(beta) = opposite/hypotenuse = AH/AB.
Therefore AH = AB * sin(beta).
keyConcept: The altitude to a side equals a bordering side times the sine of the adjacent base angle.
commonMistake: Pairing side AC with angle beta; AC must be paired with its own angle gamma (AH = AC * sin gamma).

optionExplanations.0: AC * tan(gamma) does not equal AH; tangent uses the leg on BC, not the hypotenuse relation.
optionExplanations.2: AC * cos(gamma) gives the projection CH onto BC, not the altitude.
optionExplanations.3: AC * sin(beta) mismatches the side and angle; it should be AC * sin(gamma).

shortExplanation: The square-root symbol denotes the non-negative principal root, so sqrt(x) = 4 gives the single solution x = 16.
solutionSteps: sqrt(x) means the principal (non-negative) square root.
Set sqrt(x) = 4 and square both sides: x = 16.
Check: sqrt(16) = 4, valid; there is exactly one solution.
keyConcept: The radical sign yields only the non-negative root, so an equation like sqrt(x) = k>0 has one solution.
commonMistake: Adding a spurious x = -4 (that comes from x^2 = 16, a different equation).

optionExplanations.1: 'two positive solutions' is impossible since squaring gives a unique x.
optionExplanations.2: 'two solutions of opposite sign' confuses this with x^2 = 16.
optionExplanations.4: 'no real solution' is wrong; x = 16 works.

formulaNotes: sqrt(x) = k (k>=0) has the unique solution x = k^2.

keyConcept: Rewrite all factors on a common base, then add exponents when multiplying like bases.
commonMistake: Getting 3^9 by forgetting the extra factor of 3 in 'three times'.

optionExplanations.0: 3^9 equals 27^3 alone, omitting the leading factor of 3.
optionExplanations.3: 3^7 uses an incorrect exponent chain.
optionExplanations.4: 81^3 = 3^12, larger than the correct 3^10.

shortExplanation: The given line has slope 1/2, so the perpendicular slope is -2; through (2,1) this gives y = -2x + 5, i.e. 2x + y - 5 = 0.
solutionSteps: Given slope = 1/2, so the perpendicular slope = -1/(1/2) = -2.
Point-slope through (2,1): y - 1 = -2(x - 2).
Simplify: y = -2x + 4 + 1 = -2x + 5.
Rearrange to 2x + y - 5 = 0.
keyConcept: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals; then apply point-slope form.
commonMistake: Using slope +2 or 1/2 instead of the negative reciprocal -2.

optionExplanations.1: x + 2y - 4 = 0 has slope -1/2, not perpendicular to a slope-1/2 line.
optionExplanations.2: x - 2y = 0 has slope 1/2, parallel (not perpendicular) to the given line.
optionExplanations.3: 2x + y - 4 = 0 has the right slope but does not pass through (2,1): 4+1-4 = 1 ≠ 0.

shortExplanation: Factor sin(2x) - cos(x) = cos(x)(2 sin x - 1); it is zero whenever cos(x) = 0, which includes x = ±pi/2 + 2k*pi. So those values satisfy sin(2x) - cos(x) = 0.
solutionSteps: At x = ±pi/2 + 2k*pi we have cos(x) = 0 and sin(x) = ±1.
Use sin(2x) = 2 sin(x) cos(x), so sin(2x) - cos(x) = cos(x)(2 sin x - 1).
Since cos(x) = 0 at these points, the whole expression is 0.
Hence x = ±pi/2 + 2k*pi are solutions of sin(2x) - cos(x) = 0.
keyConcept: Test candidate angles by evaluating cos and sin, using double-angle identities to simplify.
commonMistake: Overlooking that tan(x) and cot(2x) are undefined at x = pi/2, which disqualifies several options.

optionExplanations.0: tan(2x) = 3 tan(x) is undefined at x = pi/2 because tan(x) does not exist there.
optionExplanations.2: cos(x) + cos(2x) at x = pi/2 gives 0 + (-1) = -1 ≠ 0.
optionExplanations.3: sin(x) + sin(2x) at x = pi/2 gives 1 + 0 = 1 ≠ 0.

shortExplanation: By the factor theorem, saying 1 is a zero means P(1) = 0, which is equivalent to P(x) being divisible by (x - 1).
solutionSteps: A number a is a zero of P means P(a) = 0.
The factor theorem: P(a) = 0 <=> (x - a) divides P(x).
With a = 1, this means (x - 1) divides P(x).
Indeed P(1) = 3 - 3 + 2 - 2 = 0 confirms it.
keyConcept: Factor theorem: a is a root of P <=> (x - a) is a factor of P.
commonMistake: Using the factor (x + 1) instead of (x - 1) for the root x = 1.

optionExplanations.0: 'P(x) - 1 = 0 for every x' misreads the meaning of a zero.
optionExplanations.1: Divisibility by x + 1 corresponds to the root x = -1, not x = 1.
optionExplanations.4: This cubic does not have three real roots (only x = 1 is real), so that statement is false.

shortExplanation: Three lines in general position (pairwise intersecting, not concurrent) form a triangle and divide the plane into 7 regions.
solutionSteps: Start with the plane as 1 region.
Each new line in general position adds (number of the line) regions: line 1 adds 1, line 2 adds 2, line 3 adds 3.
Total regions = 1 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 7.
Equivalently 1 + n + C(n,2) with n = 3 gives 1 + 3 + 3 = 7.
keyConcept: n lines in general position split the plane into 1 + n + C(n,2) regions.
commonMistake: Counting 6 by forgetting the central triangular region formed by the three lines.

optionExplanations.0: 4 would be the count for two intersecting lines, not three.
optionExplanations.2: 6 undercounts by missing the inner triangle region.
optionExplanations.4: 8 overcounts; general-position 3 lines give exactly 7.

formulaNotes: Regions = 1 + n + n(n-1)/2 for n lines in general position.

shortExplanation: Among 1, 25, pi, sqrt(3/8), 8/3, cbrt(8/27), the rationals are 1, 25, 8/3 and cbrt(8/27) = 2/3, so four are rational.
solutionSteps: 1 is rational (integer).
25 is rational (integer).
pi is irrational.
sqrt(3/8) = sqrt(6)/4 is irrational (3/8 is not a perfect-square ratio).
8/3 is rational.
cbrt(8/27) = 2/3 is rational.
Count the rationals: 1, 25, 8/3, 2/3 => four.
keyConcept: A root is rational only when the radicand is a perfect power of the matching index.
commonMistake: Treating sqrt(3/8) as rational, or forgetting cbrt(8/27) simplifies neatly to 2/3.

optionExplanations.1: 'Two' ignores that both 8/3 and cbrt(8/27) are also rational.
optionExplanations.2: 'Three' misses one of the four rationals.
optionExplanations.4: 'Five' wrongly counts an irrational (pi or sqrt(3/8)) as rational.

shortExplanation: With ratio 1:5 the numbers are 15 and 75 (since 6 parts sum to 90), so their difference is 75 - 15 = 60.
solutionSteps: Let the numbers be x and 5x.
The numbers are 15 and 75.
Difference = 75 - 15 = 60.
keyConcept: Express ratio quantities with a common multiple, solve from the sum, then subtract.
commonMistake: Reporting the smaller number (15) or a part value instead of the difference.

optionExplanations.0: 45 would be the difference only if the split were 22.5 and 67.5, not a 1:5 ratio.
optionExplanations.1: 18 does not arise from any correct step here.
optionExplanations.3: 75 is the larger number itself, not the difference.

formulaNotes: For ratio 1:5 with sum S, numbers are S/6 and 5S/6; difference = 4S/6 = 2S/3 = 60.

shortExplanation: The volume between the concentric spheres is (4/3)*pi*(R^3 - r^3) = (4/3)*pi*(8 - 1) = 28*pi/3 cm^3.
solutionSteps: Volume of a sphere = (4/3)*pi*radius^3.
Outer sphere: (4/3)*pi*2^3 = (32/3)*pi.
Inner sphere: (4/3)*pi*1^3 = (4/3)*pi.
Difference = (4/3)*pi*(8 - 1) = 28*pi/3 cm^3.
keyConcept: The shell volume between concentric spheres is (4/3)*pi*(R^3 - r^3).
commonMistake: Dropping the factor pi or subtracting radii instead of their cubes.

optionExplanations.0: 14/3 has no pi and uses a wrong constant.
optionExplanations.1: 28/3 is missing the factor pi.
optionExplanations.3: 2*pi/3 comes from an incorrect radius-difference computation.

shortExplanation: Since x^2+1 is always at least 1, its reciprocal 1/(x^2+1) is always positive and at most 1, reaching 1 only at x=0. The range is (0, 1].
solutionSteps: Note x^2 >= 0 for all real x, so x^2+1 >= 1.
Taking the reciprocal reverses the inequality for positive values: 0 < 1/(x^2+1) <= 1.
The maximum 1 is attained at x=0; the value approaches 0 as |x| grows but never equals 0.
Therefore the range is (0, 1].
keyConcept: The range of 1/(x^2+1) follows from bounding the denominator x^2+1 >= 1.
commonMistake: Including 0 in the range, even though the function is never actually 0.

optionExplanations.1: This wrongly includes 0, but 1/(x^2+1) is never equal to 0.
optionExplanations.2: The values never exceed 1, since the denominator is at least 1.
optionExplanations.3: The output is bounded above by 1, so it cannot go to infinity.

formulaNotes: For x^2+1 in [1, infinity), 1/(x^2+1) lies in (0, 1].

shortExplanation: Variance grows with the spread of values about the mean. The set {-2, 0, 2} is symmetric with the widest spread, giving the greatest variance.
solutionSteps: Each listed set has mean 0 except {2,1,2} (mean 5/3).
The largest value, 8/3, belongs to {-2,0,2}.
keyConcept: Variance measures average squared deviation from the mean; wider symmetric spread means larger variance.
commonMistake: Judging by the largest single value rather than the spread of deviations from the mean.

optionExplanations.0: {-1,0,1} has spread only half as wide, giving variance 2/3.
optionExplanations.3: {-1,0,2} has variance about 1.56, smaller than 8/3.
optionExplanations.4: {2,1,2} is tightly clustered, giving the smallest variance.

shortExplanation: The expression factors as a perfect square (x-1)^2 = 0, so the only solution is x = 1.
solutionSteps: Recognize x^2 - 2x + 1 = (x-1)^2.
Solve x - 1 = 0, giving x = 1 (a double root).
keyConcept: A perfect-square trinomial has a single repeated root.
commonMistake: Expecting two distinct roots when the discriminant is zero.

optionExplanations.0: Substituting x=0 gives 1, not 0, so it is not a root.
optionExplanations.2: Substituting x=-1 gives 1+2+1=4, not 0.
optionExplanations.3: Substituting x=2 gives 4-4+1=1, not 0.

shortExplanation: By Vieta's formulas, the sum of the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 equals -b/a.
solutionSteps: For roots r1 and r2, r1 + r2 = -b/a and r1*r2 = c/a.
The sum is therefore -b/a.
keyConcept: Vieta's formulas relate coefficients to sums and products of roots.
commonMistake: Confusing the sum of roots (-b/a) with the product of roots (c/a).

optionExplanations.0: -c/a is neither the sum nor the product of the roots.
optionExplanations.2: The sign is wrong; the sum is -b/a, not b/a.
optionExplanations.3: c/a is the product of the roots, not their sum.

formulaNotes: Sum of roots = -b/a; product of roots = c/a.

shortExplanation: Solving y = 2x + 3 for x gives x = (y-3)/2, so the inverse is f^-1(x) = (x-3)/2.
solutionSteps: Write y = 2x + 3.
Subtract 3: y - 3 = 2x.
Divide by 2: x = (y-3)/2.
Swap variable name: f^-1(x) = (x-3)/2.
keyConcept: Find an inverse by solving y = f(x) for x, then renaming.
commonMistake: Adding 3 instead of subtracting, giving (x+3)/2.

optionExplanations.0: (x+3)/2 reverses the sign of the constant; check f(f^-1(x)) fails.
optionExplanations.2: 2x - 3 is not the inverse; f(2x-3) does not return x.
optionExplanations.4: 2x + 3 is the original function, not its inverse.

shortExplanation: The whole quantity 3 sin x is squared, so (3 sin x)^2 is the square of the triple of the sine of x.
solutionSteps: Identify the inner quantity: 3 sin x is three times the sine of x (the triple of the sine of x).
The square applies to that entire quantity: (3 sin x)^2.
So it reads as the square of the triple of the sine of x.
keyConcept: Parentheses show the squaring applies to the whole product 3 sin x.
commonMistake: Confusing (3 sin x)^2 = 9 sin^2 x with 3 sin^2 x (only the sine squared).

optionExplanations.1: The triple of the sine of the square of x would be 3 sin(x^2), unrelated.
optionExplanations.2: The triple of the square of the sine would be 3 sin^2 x, not (3 sin x)^2.
optionExplanations.3: The square of the sine of the triple of x would be sin^2(3x), a different expression.

shortExplanation: A single real root requires discriminant zero: 36 - 4k = 0, so k = 9.
solutionSteps: Discriminant of x^2 - 6x + k is (-6)^2 - 4(1)(k) = 36 - 4k.
Set it to 0 for exactly one real root: 36 - 4k = 0.
Solve: k = 9.
keyConcept: A quadratic has exactly one real root when its discriminant equals zero.
commonMistake: Setting the discriminant to something other than zero, or dropping the factor 4.

optionExplanations.1: k=6 gives discriminant 36-24=12 > 0, so two distinct roots.
optionExplanations.2: k=3 gives discriminant 24 > 0, two roots.
optionExplanations.3: k=12 gives discriminant 36-48=-12 < 0, no real roots.

formulaNotes: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac; one real root when it equals 0.

solutionSteps: Subtract: 86 - 53 = 33.
keyConcept: Evaluate the closed-form term at two indices and subtract.
commonMistake: Arithmetic slips such as forgetting to square n or misapplying the -3n term.

optionExplanations.0: 25 ignores the linear/constant contributions.
optionExplanations.1: 31 results from a miscalculation of one of the two terms.
optionExplanations.3: 37 would come from an error in the squared component.

shortExplanation: log base 5 equal to 2 means the argument equals 5^2 = 25, so 2x - 1 = 25 and x = 13.
solutionSteps: Rewrite in exponential form: 2x - 1 = 5^2 = 25.
Divide by 2: x = 13.
Check: 2(13)-1 = 25 > 0, valid for the logarithm.
keyConcept: log_b(A) = c is equivalent to A = b^c.
commonMistake: Treating 5^2 as 10 or forgetting to isolate x after exponentiating.

optionExplanations.0: x=6 gives argument 11, and log_5(11) is not 2.
optionExplanations.2: x=8 gives argument 15, not 25.
optionExplanations.3: x=9 gives argument 17, not 25.

shortExplanation: By the Pythagorean identity, sin^2(t) + cos^2(t) = 1 for any angle, so the value is 1.
solutionSteps: Apply the identity sin^2(theta) + cos^2(theta) = 1.
This holds for every angle, including 45 degrees.
Therefore the value is 1.
keyConcept: The fundamental Pythagorean identity holds for all angles.
commonMistake: Computing each term as (sqrt2/2)^2 = 1/2 and stopping at 0.5 instead of adding both.

optionExplanations.0: 0.5 is the value of just one squared term, not their sum.
optionExplanations.2: 1.5 is not consistent with the identity, which fixes the sum at 1.
optionExplanations.3: 2 would arise from doubling incorrectly.

shortExplanation: From (4/3)*pi*r^3 = 36*pi, dividing by pi and multiplying by 3/4 gives r^3 = 27, so r = 3 cm.
solutionSteps: Set the sphere-volume formula equal to the given volume: (4/3)*pi*r^3 = 36*pi.
Divide both sides by pi: (4/3)*r^3 = 36.
Multiply both sides by 3/4: r^3 = 27.
Take the cube root: r = 3 cm.
keyConcept: Sphere volume is (4/3)*pi*r^3; solve for the radius by isolating r^3 and taking a cube root.
commonMistake: Dropping the 4/3 factor, or taking a square root instead of a cube root of 27.

optionExplanations.0: r = 2 gives volume (4/3)*pi*8 = (32/3)*pi ~ 10.67*pi, not 36*pi.
optionExplanations.2: r = 4 gives (4/3)*pi*64 = (256/3)*pi ~ 85.3*pi, far larger than 36*pi.
optionExplanations.3: r = 5 gives (4/3)*pi*125 = (500/3)*pi ~ 166.7*pi, much too large.
optionExplanations.4: r = 6 gives (4/3)*pi*216 = 288*pi, hugely larger than 36*pi.

shortExplanation: Dividing by (x-1) leaves x^2 - 5x + 6 = (x-2)(x-3), so the roots are 1, 2, 3.
solutionSteps: Given root 1, divide x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 by (x-1).
The quotient is x^2 - 5x + 6.
The full root set is {1, 2, 3}.
keyConcept: Factor out the known root, then solve the remaining quadratic.
commonMistake: Guessing consecutive integers without verifying they multiply to the constant term 6.

optionExplanations.1: 1*3*4 = 12, not equal to the constant 6, so these cannot be the roots.
optionExplanations.2: 1*4*5 = 20, inconsistent with the product of roots.
optionExplanations.3: 1*5*6 = 30, far from the required product 6.

shortExplanation: Using point-slope y - 2 = (-2/3)(x + 1) and setting x = 0 gives y = 4/3.
solutionSteps: Write point-slope form: y - 2 = (-2/3)(x - (-1)) = (-2/3)(x + 1).
Set x = 0 to find the y-intercept: y - 2 = (-2/3)(1) = -2/3.
keyConcept: The y-intercept is the y-value when x = 0 on the line.
commonMistake: Using the wrong sign for the point (-1, 2) when substituting into the slope formula.

optionExplanations.0: 8/3 comes from adding 2/3 instead of subtracting it.
optionExplanations.3: -2/3 is the slope-times-run term, not the intercept.
optionExplanations.4: -4/3 has the wrong sign for the intercept.

formulaNotes: y = m*x + b with m = -2/3 through (-1,2) gives b = 4/3.

shortExplanation: tan 15 = tan(45 - 30) = (1 - 1/sqrt3)/(1 + 1/sqrt3), which simplifies to 2 - sqrt3.
solutionSteps: Write 15 = 45 - 30 and use tan(A-B) = (tanA - tanB)/(1 + tanA tanB).
Substitute tan45 = 1, tan30 = 1/sqrt3: (1 - 1/sqrt3)/(1 + 1/sqrt3).
Multiply numerator and denominator by sqrt3: (sqrt3 - 1)/(sqrt3 + 1).
Rationalize by multiplying by (sqrt3 - 1)/(sqrt3 - 1): (3 - 2sqrt3 + 1)/(3 - 1) = (4 - 2sqrt3)/2 = 2 - sqrt3.
keyConcept: The tangent subtraction formula converts tan 15 into known 45 and 30 values.
commonMistake: Forgetting to rationalize the denominator, leaving an unsimplified fraction.

optionExplanations.0: 2 + sqrt3 is tan 75, the complementary angle, not tan 15.
optionExplanations.2: sqrt3 + 1 is far larger than tan 15 ≈ 0.27.
optionExplanations.3: sqrt3 - 1 is not equal to 2 - sqrt3 numerically (0.73 vs 0.27).

formulaNotes: tan(A-B) = (tanA - tanB)/(1 + tanA tanB); tan15 = 2 - sqrt3 ≈ 0.268.

shortExplanation: The probability is (5/8) for the first red times (4/7) for the second, giving 20/56 = 5/14.
solutionSteps: First draw red: 5 red out of 8 total = 5/8.
Without replacement, second draw red: 4 red out of 7 remaining = 4/7.
keyConcept: For dependent draws without replacement, multiply conditional probabilities.
commonMistake: Using 5/8 twice (as if with replacement) instead of updating to 4/7.

optionExplanations.0: 5/8 is only the probability of the first draw being red.
optionExplanations.2: 2/7 does not match the product of the two conditional probabilities.
optionExplanations.3: 1/4 would require different counts; the correct product is 5/14.

shortExplanation: With radius fixed, volume is proportional to height, so a 20% volume increase requires a 20% height increase: 10*1.2 = 12 cm.
solutionSteps: Cylinder volume V = pi*r^2*h; with r constant, V is proportional to h.
Increasing V by 20% means h must increase by 20%.
New height = 10 * 1.20 = 12 cm.
keyConcept: With a fixed radius, cylinder volume scales linearly with height.
commonMistake: Adding 20% of the radius or misapplying the percentage to the wrong dimension.

optionExplanations.0: 11 cm is only a 10% increase, not 20%.
optionExplanations.2: 13 cm is a 30% increase in height.
optionExplanations.4: 15 cm is a 50% increase, far more than 20%.

formulaNotes: V = pi*r^2*h; constant r means h_new = 1.2*h = 12 cm.

shortExplanation: An absolute value changes formula depending on the sign inside. Split the number line at the points where each inside-expression turns from negative to positive, solve on each piece, and only x = 1 both works and appears in the options.
solutionSteps: The absolute value |A| equals A when A is positive or zero, and equals -A when A is negative. So the two bars here change behavior at the points where each inside becomes zero.
2x + 1 = 0 at x = -1/2, and x - 1 = 0 at x = 1. These two points cut the number line into three regions to check.
Region x > 1: both insides are positive, so |2x+1| + |x-1| = (2x+1) + (x-1) = 3x. Setting 3x = 3 gives x = 1, but that is not inside 'x greater than 1', so reject it here.
Region -1/2 <= x <= 1: here 2x+1 is positive but x-1 is negative, so the equation is (2x+1) + (1-x) = x + 2. Setting x + 2 = 3 gives x = 1, which does lie in this region. Valid: x = 1.
Region x < -1/2: both insides are negative, so we get -(2x+1) + (1-x) = -3x. Setting -3x = 3 gives x = -1, which is indeed less than -1/2. Valid: x = -1.
So the full solution set is x = 1 and x = -1. Among the five choices, only x = 1 appears, so that is the answer.
keyConcept: To solve an equation with absolute values, break the number line at every point where an inside expression equals zero, drop the bars using the correct sign on each piece, solve, and keep only solutions that actually land in the region you assumed.
commonMistake: Guessing by plugging in the answer choices. That can miss solutions the test does not list (here x = -1 also works) and it never teaches you the method. It also tempts you to drop a bar and treat a term as always positive, which quietly breaks the equation.

optionExplanations.1: x = 2 gives |5| + |1| = 6, not 3. Too large; the left side keeps growing once x passes 1.

formulaNotes: |A| = A when A >= 0, and |A| = -A when A < 0. Break points here: 2x+1=0 -> x=-1/2, and x-1=0 -> x=1.

shortExplanation: For y^2 = 4px with 4p = 8, we get p = 2, so the focus is at (2, 0).
solutionSteps: Compare y^2 = 8x to the standard form y^2 = 4px.
Then 4p = 8, so p = 2.
The focus of y^2 = 4px is at (p, 0) = (2, 0).
keyConcept: For y^2 = 4px, the focus lies at (p, 0) on the axis of symmetry.
commonMistake: Placing the focus on the y-axis, though this parabola opens along the x-axis.

optionExplanations.1: (0,2) lies on the y-axis, but this parabola's focus is on the x-axis.
optionExplanations.2: (-2,0) has the wrong sign; the parabola opens to the right.
optionExplanations.4: (1,0) would require 4p = 4, but here 4p = 8.

shortExplanation: After adding 13, the ordered set has 7 values, and the median is the 4th, which is 7.
solutionSteps: New set: {1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13}, already sorted, with 7 elements.
The median of 7 values is the 4th value.
The 4th value is 7.
keyConcept: For an odd count n, the median is the ((n+1)/2)-th ordered value.
commonMistake: Averaging the two middle values as if the count were still even.

optionExplanations.0: 6 was the median of the original 6-element set, before adding 13.
optionExplanations.2: 8 does not appear as a middle value in the 7-element ordered set.
optionExplanations.3: 9 is the 5th value, not the middle one.

solutionSteps: Add the bases: 8 + 12 = 20.
Multiply by the height: 20 * 5 = 100.
Take half: 100 / 2 = 50 cm^2.
keyConcept: Trapezoid area is the average of the parallel bases times the height.
commonMistake: Forgetting the factor 1/2 and reporting 100 cm^2.

optionExplanations.0: 40 cm^2 would use an incorrect base sum or height.
optionExplanations.2: 60 cm^2 does not match (1/2)(20)(5) = 50.
optionExplanations.4: 80 cm^2 overestimates the area.

shortExplanation: Sums greater than 9 (10, 11, 12) occur in 6 of the 36 equally likely outcomes, giving probability 6/36 = 1/6.
solutionSteps: Total outcomes for two dice: 6*6 = 36.
Favorable = 3+2+1 = 6, so probability = 6/36 = 1/6.
keyConcept: Count favorable ordered outcomes over the 36 equally likely results.
commonMistake: Interpreting 'greater than 9' as including sum 9, or missing ordered pairs.

optionExplanations.1: 1/9 = 4/36 undercounts the favorable outcomes.
optionExplanations.2: 1/12 = 3/36 counts only one of the three sums.
optionExplanations.4: 1/36 counts only the single outcome (6,6).

shortExplanation: Volume 27 gives side 3, and surface area = 6*side^2 = 6*9 = 54 cm^2.
solutionSteps: Side length: cube root of 27 = 3 cm.
One face area: 3^2 = 9 cm^2.
Total surface area: 6 * 9 = 54 cm^2.
keyConcept: A cube's surface area is 6 times the square of its edge length.
commonMistake: Using 4 faces instead of 6, or confusing volume and area.

optionExplanations.0: 36 cm^2 uses only 4 faces (4*9), not all 6.
optionExplanations.2: 72 cm^2 would require 8 faces.
optionExplanations.3: 108 cm^2 doubles the correct surface area.

formulaNotes: SA = 6*a^2 with a = 3, so SA = 54 cm^2.

shortExplanation: Factoring gives (x-2)(x-3) < 0, which holds between the roots: 2 < x < 3.
solutionSteps: The product of two factors is negative between the roots 2 and 3.
Solution: 2 < x < 3.
keyConcept: A downward-signed product of linear factors is negative between its roots.
commonMistake: Reversing the inequality direction or including the endpoints where the expression equals 0.

optionExplanations.1: 1 < x < 4 is too wide; the expression is positive outside (2,3).
optionExplanations.2: 0 < x < 5 includes regions where the expression is positive.
optionExplanations.4: 3 < x < 6 lies entirely where the expression is positive.

shortExplanation: cos 15 = cos(45 - 30) = cos45 cos30 + sin45 sin30 = (sqrt6 + sqrt2)/4.
solutionSteps: Write 15 = 45 - 30 and use cos(A-B) = cosA cosB + sinA sinB.
Substitute: (sqrt2/2)(sqrt3/2) + (sqrt2/2)(1/2).
Combine: sqrt6/4 + sqrt2/4 = (sqrt6 + sqrt2)/4.
keyConcept: The cosine subtraction formula gives exact values for 15 degrees.
commonMistake: Using a minus sign, which yields cos 75 = (sqrt6 - sqrt2)/4 instead.

optionExplanations.1: (sqrt6 - sqrt2)/4 is cos 75 (or sin 15), not cos 15.
optionExplanations.2: (sqrt2 + sqrt3)/2 exceeds 1 and cannot be a cosine value.
optionExplanations.4: sqrt2/2 is cos 45, not cos 15.

formulaNotes: cos(A-B) = cosA cosB + sinA sinB; cos15 = (sqrt6 + sqrt2)/4 ≈ 0.966.

shortExplanation: Volume = (1/3)*base area*height = (1/3)*16*6 = 32 cm^3.
solutionSteps: Base area of the square: 4^2 = 16 cm^2.
Apply the pyramid formula: V = (1/3)*base*height = (1/3)*16*6.
keyConcept: A pyramid's volume is one-third the base area times the height.
commonMistake: Omitting the 1/3 factor and reporting 96 cm^3.

optionExplanations.0: 24 cm^3 would use a base area of 12, not 16.
optionExplanations.2: 48 cm^3 uses a factor 1/2 instead of 1/3.
optionExplanations.4: 96 cm^3 omits the 1/3 factor entirely.

shortExplanation: Factor the numerator and cancel the common factor. For x not equal to 2 the expression simplifies to x + 2, and the inequality requires x + 2 <= 0, giving x <= -2.
solutionSteps: For x not equal to 2, (x-2)(x+2)/(x-2) = x + 2.
Solve x + 2 <= 0, giving x <= -2.
x = 2 is excluded from the domain but is not in x <= -2 anyway, so the solution stays x <= -2.
keyConcept: Cancel a common factor only after excluding the value that makes the denominator zero.
commonMistake: Forgetting the domain restriction x not equal to 2 or keeping the point x = 2 in the solution set.

optionExplanations.1: -2 < x < 2 is where x + 2 is positive, so the expression is > 0 there, not <= 0.
optionExplanations.2: x <= 2 wrongly includes the excluded point x = 2 and the whole interval where the expression is positive.
optionExplanations.3: x < -2 or x >= 2 mixes an unrelated interval and includes the forbidden value x = 2.

shortExplanation: A circle with center (h, k) and radius r has equation (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2. Substituting (-1, 3) and r = 5 gives (x + 1)^2 + (y - 3)^2 = 25.
solutionSteps: Write the standard form (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2.
Substitute h = -1 and k = 3: (x - (-1))^2 + (y - 3)^2.
Square the radius: r^2 = 5^2 = 25.
keyConcept: The signs of the center coordinates flip inside the squared terms, and the constant is r squared.
commonMistake: Using r instead of r^2 on the right side, or copying the center signs without flipping them.

optionExplanations.1: (x - 1)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 25 uses center (1, -3), the sign of both coordinates reversed.
optionExplanations.2: (x + 1)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 5 has the wrong y-sign and uses r instead of r^2.
optionExplanations.4: (x + 3)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 25 swaps the coordinates of the center.

shortExplanation: 135 degrees lies in the second quadrant where tangent is negative, and its reference angle is 45 degrees, so tan(135) = -tan(45) = -1.
solutionSteps: Write 135 = 180 - 45, a second-quadrant angle.
The reference angle is 45 degrees.
Tangent is negative in the second quadrant.
keyConcept: Use the reference angle plus the sign of the trig function in the given quadrant.
commonMistake: Forgetting the negative sign because tangent is negative in the second quadrant.

optionExplanations.0: -sqrt(2) is not a value of tangent at any standard angle here.
optionExplanations.3: 1 is tan(45) but ignores the second-quadrant sign.
optionExplanations.4: -sqrt(3)/3 equals tan(150), not tan(135).

shortExplanation: There are 2^3 = 8 equally likely outcomes, and exactly 2 heads occurs in C(3,2) = 3 of them, so the probability is 3/8.
solutionSteps: Total outcomes for 3 flips: 2^3 = 8.
Count arrangements of exactly 2 heads: C(3,2) = 3.
Divide favorable by total: 3/8.
keyConcept: Binomial counting: choose which flips are heads with C(n, k).
commonMistake: Treating the number of heads as equally likely and answering 1/4, or forgetting the 3 arrangements.

optionExplanations.0: 1/4 would be the count 2 out of 8, but there are 3 favorable arrangements not 2.
optionExplanations.2: 1/2 ignores that exactly 2 heads is more restrictive than getting any majority.
optionExplanations.4: 1/8 is the probability of one specific outcome such as all heads, not exactly 2 heads.

formulaNotes: P = C(n, k) / 2^n with n = 3, k = 2.

shortExplanation: The lateral surface area of a cone is pi * r * l. With r = 4 and l = 5 this is pi * 4 * 5 = 20*pi cm^2.
solutionSteps: Recall lateral area = pi * r * l.
Substitute r = 4 and slant height l = 5.
Compute pi * 4 * 5 = 20*pi cm^2.
keyConcept: The lateral (curved) surface of a cone uses the slant height, not the vertical height.
commonMistake: Adding the base area (pi*r^2 = 16*pi) to get total surface, or using height instead of slant height.

optionExplanations.1: 25*pi would be pi*r*l with the wrong values or an added constant.
optionExplanations.2: 30*pi does not match pi*4*5.
optionExplanations.3: 40*pi doubles the correct value, as if using diameter instead of radius.

formulaNotes: Lateral area of cone = pi * r * l.

shortExplanation: Factor as (x + 5)(x - 2) > 0. The product is positive outside the roots, so x < -5 or x > 2.
solutionSteps: Find roots x = -5 and x = 2.
A positive product occurs outside the roots.
Solution: x < -5 or x > 2.
keyConcept: An upward parabola is positive outside its two roots and negative between them.
commonMistake: Reporting the between-roots interval, which is where the expression is negative.

optionExplanations.1: -5 < x < 2 is exactly where the expression is negative.
optionExplanations.2: x < -2 or x > 5 uses the wrong roots.
optionExplanations.3: -2 < x < 5 uses wrong roots and the wrong interval direction.

shortExplanation: Writing x^2 = 4py gives 4p = -4, so p = -1 and the parabola opens downward. The directrix is y = -p = 1.
solutionSteps: Match x^2 = -4y to x^2 = 4py, so 4p = -4 and p = -1.
Focus is at (0, p) = (0, -1); the parabola opens downward.
The directrix is the horizontal line y = -p.
y = -(-1) = 1, so directrix is y = 1.
keyConcept: For x^2 = 4py the directrix is y = -p, on the opposite side of the vertex from the focus.
commonMistake: Confusing the directrix line y = 1 with the focus line y = -1, or using a vertical line.

optionExplanations.1: y = -1 is the location of the focus, not the directrix.
optionExplanations.2: x = 1 is vertical; this parabola opens along the y-axis so the directrix is horizontal.
optionExplanations.4: y = 0 is the vertex line, not the directrix.

shortExplanation: 150 degrees is in the second quadrant with reference angle 30 degrees, and sine is positive there, so sin(150) = sin(30) = 1/2.
solutionSteps: Reference angle is 30 degrees.
Sine is positive in the second quadrant.
keyConcept: sin(180 - x) = sin(x); sine stays positive in the second quadrant.
commonMistake: Assigning a negative sign or confusing sine with cosine (which would give -sqrt(3)/2).

optionExplanations.1: -1/2 wrongly makes sine negative in the second quadrant.
optionExplanations.2: sqrt(3)/2 is sin(120) or cos(30), not sin(150).
optionExplanations.3: -sqrt(3)/2 is cos(150), not sin(150).

shortExplanation: The mode is the most frequent value. Here 5 appears three times, more than any other value, so the mode is 5.
solutionSteps: Count frequencies: 2 appears twice, 4 appears twice, 5 appears three times.
Identify the highest frequency: 5 occurs three times.
The mode is 5.
keyConcept: Mode = value with the greatest frequency in the data set.
commonMistake: Confusing mode with median or picking a value that ties at a lower count.

optionExplanations.0: 2 appears only twice, fewer than 5.
optionExplanations.2: 4 appears only twice, fewer than 5.
optionExplanations.4: 2 and 4 each appear twice, but 5 appears more often, so the set is not bimodal at 2 and 4.

shortExplanation: Total surface area = 2(lw + lh + wh) = 2(3*4 + 4*5 + 3*5) = 2(47) = 94 cm^2.
solutionSteps: List the three distinct face products: 3*4 = 12, 4*5 = 20, 3*5 = 15.
Double for the paired faces: 2 * 47 = 94 cm^2.
keyConcept: A box has three pairs of congruent faces; sum their areas and double.
commonMistake: Forgetting to double, or computing volume (3*4*5 = 60) instead of surface area.

optionExplanations.1: 96 comes from an arithmetic slip in the face sum.
optionExplanations.2: 98 overcounts the face areas.
optionExplanations.3: 100 does not match 2(12 + 20 + 15).

shortExplanation: Rewrite in exponential form: x^2 + 7 = 2^3 = 8, so x^2 = 1 and x = 1 (the positive root offered).
solutionSteps: Convert log_2(x^2 + 7) = 3 to x^2 + 7 = 2^3.
x^2 = 1, giving x = 1 or x = -1.
The listed solution is x = 1.
keyConcept: log_b(A) = c is equivalent to A = b^c.
commonMistake: Multiplying instead of exponentiating, or forgetting to subtract 7 before taking the root.

optionExplanations.1: x = 2 gives x^2 + 7 = 11, whose log base 2 is not 3.
optionExplanations.2: x = 3 gives x^2 + 7 = 16 = 2^4, so the log would be 4, not 3.
optionExplanations.3: x = 4 gives x^2 + 7 = 23, not a power of 2.

shortExplanation: The midpoint is the average of the coordinates: ((2 + 6)/2, (-3 + 5)/2) = (4, 1).
solutionSteps: Average the x-coordinates: (2 + 6)/2 = 4.
Average the y-coordinates: (-3 + 5)/2 = 1.
Midpoint is (4, 1).
keyConcept: Midpoint = componentwise average of the two endpoints.
commonMistake: Subtracting coordinates instead of averaging, or swapping x and y.

optionExplanations.1: (4, -1) uses the wrong sign for the averaged y-value.
optionExplanations.2: (-4, 1) negates the correct x-value.
optionExplanations.4: (1, 4) swaps the x and y results.

shortExplanation: By inclusion-exclusion, P(heart or king) = 13/52 + 4/52 - 1/52 = 16/52, subtracting the king of hearts counted twice.
solutionSteps: Hearts: 13 cards. Kings: 4 cards.
The king of hearts is in both sets, so subtract 1 overlap.
Favorable = 13 + 4 - 1 = 16.
Probability = 16/52.
keyConcept: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B).
commonMistake: Adding 13 + 4 = 17 without subtracting the shared king of hearts.

optionExplanations.1: 13/52 counts only hearts, ignoring the other kings.
optionExplanations.3: 17/52 double-counts the king of hearts.
optionExplanations.4: 26/52 corresponds to a color (all red cards), not hearts-or-kings.

formulaNotes: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B).

shortExplanation: From surface area 4*pi*r^2 = 36*pi we get r = 3, and volume (4/3)*pi*r^3 = (4/3)*pi*27 = 36*pi cm^3.
solutionSteps: Set 4*pi*r^2 = 36*pi, so r^2 = 9 and r = 3.
Apply volume V = (4/3)*pi*r^3.
keyConcept: Find r from the surface-area formula, then substitute into the volume formula.
commonMistake: Using r^2 = 36 instead of solving 4*pi*r^2 = 36*pi, or miscubing the radius.

optionExplanations.1: 48*pi does not match (4/3)*pi*27.
optionExplanations.3: 72*pi doubles the correct volume.
optionExplanations.4: 108*pi is 4*pi*r^3, missing the 1/3 factor.

shortExplanation: The axis of symmetry is x = -b/(2a). With a = -1 and b = 6 this is x = -6/(-2) = 3.
solutionSteps: Identify a = -1, b = 6 in y = -x^2 + 6x - 8.
Apply x = -b/(2a).
keyConcept: Axis of symmetry of a parabola is the vertical line x = -b/(2a).
commonMistake: Dropping the sign of a and getting x = -3 instead of 3.

optionExplanations.1: x = -3 comes from ignoring the negative leading coefficient.
optionExplanations.2: x = 2 does not satisfy -b/(2a).
optionExplanations.4: x = 1 is not the vertex location for these coefficients.

shortExplanation: The mean is 3; squared deviations sum to 10 over 5 values gives variance 2, so the (population) standard deviation is sqrt(2) approximately 1.41.
solutionSteps: Deviations: -2, -1, 0, 1, 2; squares 4, 1, 0, 1, 4 sum to 10.
Variance = 10/5 = 2.
Standard deviation = sqrt(2) which is about 1.41.
keyConcept: Population standard deviation is the square root of the mean of squared deviations.
commonMistake: Confusing this with sample standard deviation (dividing by 4, giving about 1.58).

optionExplanations.0: 1 would require variance 1, but the variance is 2.
optionExplanations.2: 1.73 is sqrt(3), which does not match variance 2.
optionExplanations.3: 2 is the variance itself, not its square root.

formulaNotes: sigma = sqrt( (sum of (x - mean)^2) / n ) = sqrt(10/5) = sqrt(2).

shortExplanation: Cone volume is (1/3)*pi*r^2*h = (1/3)*pi*9*12 = 36*pi cm^3.
solutionSteps: Apply V = (1/3)*pi*r^2*h.
r^2 = 3^2 = 9; multiply by h = 12 to get 108.
Take one third: (1/3)*108 = 36, so V = 36*pi cm^3.
keyConcept: A cone's volume is one third of the cylinder with the same base and height.
commonMistake: Omitting the 1/3 factor (giving 108*pi) or using slant height instead of vertical height.

optionExplanations.1: 18*pi results from an arithmetic error in r^2*h.
optionExplanations.2: 24*pi does not match (1/3)*pi*9*12.
optionExplanations.4: 48*pi overstates the value; the correct product one-third of 108 is 36.

shortExplanation: This geometric series has first term a = 2/3 and ratio r = 1/3, so its sum is (2/3)/(1 - 1/3) = 1.
solutionSteps: First term: n = 1 gives 2/3^1 = 2/3.
Common ratio r = 1/3 (each term multiplies by 1/3).
Sum of infinite geometric series = a/(1 - r).
keyConcept: An infinite geometric series with |r| < 1 sums to a/(1 - r).
commonMistake: Using a = 2 instead of the actual first term 2/3, or mishandling the ratio.

optionExplanations.0: 0.5 does not equal a/(1 - r) for these values.
optionExplanations.2: 1.5 would arise from a wrong first term.
optionExplanations.4: 1.33 (about 4/3) misapplies the sum formula.

shortExplanation: Substituting u = x^2 gives u^2 - 4u + 3, minimized at u = 2 with value -1; since u = 2 is attainable (x = sqrt(2)), the minimum of f is -1.
solutionSteps: The vertex of this upward parabola is at u = -(-4)/(2*1) = 2.
u = 2 is attainable since x^2 = 2 has real solutions.
keyConcept: Substitute u = x^2 to turn a quartic in x into a quadratic, then minimize.
commonMistake: Evaluating only at x = 0 (giving 3) and missing the lower interior minimum.

optionExplanations.1: 0 is not attained by f for any real x.
optionExplanations.3: 2 is not the minimum value.
optionExplanations.4: 3 is f(0), the value at the origin, but not the global minimum.

formulaNotes: f = u^2 - 4u + 3 with u = x^2; vertex at u = 2 gives -1.

shortExplanation: The difference of cubes factors as x^3 - 8 = (x - 2)(x^2 + 2x + 4), so dividing by x - 2 leaves x^2 + 2x + 4.
solutionSteps: Recognize x^3 - 8 = x^3 - 2^3, a difference of cubes.
Cancel the (x - 2) factor (valid for x != 2).
Result: x^2 + 2x + 4.
keyConcept: Difference of cubes: a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2).
commonMistake: Using minus signs in the quadratic factor, as in x^2 - 2x + 4, which is the sum-of-cubes pattern.

optionExplanations.1: x^2 - 2x + 4 is the quotient for x^3 + 8, not x^3 - 8.
optionExplanations.2: x^2 + 4x - 2 does not multiply by (x - 2) to give x^3 - 8.
optionExplanations.3: x^2 - 4x + 2 fails the same multiplication check.

shortExplanation: The foci on the x-axis give c = 2, and the major axis length 6 gives a = 3; then b^2 = a^2 - c^2 = 9 - 4 = 5, so the ellipse is x^2/9 + y^2/5 = 1.
solutionSteps: Foci at (±2, 0) mean the major axis is horizontal and c = 2.
Major axis length 6 gives 2a = 6, so a = 3 and a^2 = 9.
Compute b^2 = a^2 - c^2 = 9 - 4 = 5.
Ellipse: x^2/9 + y^2/5 = 1.
keyConcept: For a horizontal ellipse, a^2 (under x^2) exceeds b^2, and c^2 = a^2 - b^2.
commonMistake: Putting the larger denominator under y^2, giving a vertical major axis inconsistent with x-axis foci.

optionExplanations.1: x^2/5 + y^2/9 = 1 has a vertical major axis, so its foci would lie on the y-axis.
optionExplanations.2: x^2/4 + y^2/1 = 1 gives c^2 = 3, so foci at (±sqrt(3), 0), not (±2, 0).
optionExplanations.3: x^2/1 + y^2/4 = 1 is a vertical ellipse with the wrong axis lengths.

shortExplanation: Vertices at (0, ±3) lie on the y-axis, so the hyperbola opens vertically with a^2 = 9 under y^2: y^2/9 - x^2/16 = 1.
solutionSteps: Vertices on the y-axis mean the y^2 term is positive (transverse axis vertical).
Vertex distance a = 3, so a^2 = 9 goes under y^2.
The matching form is y^2/9 - x^2/16 = 1.
keyConcept: The positive squared term identifies the transverse axis; its denominator is a^2 with vertices at distance a.
commonMistake: Putting x^2 first, which would place the vertices on the x-axis.

optionExplanations.0: x^2/9 - y^2/16 = 1 opens horizontally with vertices at (±3, 0).
optionExplanations.2: x^2/16 - y^2/9 = 1 has vertices at (±4, 0), on the x-axis.
optionExplanations.3: y^2/16 - x^2/9 = 1 opens vertically but gives vertices at (0, ±4).

shortExplanation: The vertex is at x = 3, inside [0, 4], where f(3) = -9 + 18 - 5 = 4, the maximum on the interval.
solutionSteps: Find the vertex: x = -b/(2a) = -6/(2 * -1) = 3.
x = 3 lies within [0, 4], so it gives the max of this downward parabola.
Endpoints f(0) = -5 and f(4) = 3 are smaller, confirming max = 4.
keyConcept: For a downward parabola, the vertex gives the maximum when it lies inside the interval.
commonMistake: Assuming the maximum is at an endpoint without checking the vertex inside the interval.

optionExplanations.1: 5 exceeds the vertex value; f never reaches 5 on this interval.
optionExplanations.2: 6 is above the attainable maximum of 4.
optionExplanations.3: 7 is not reached anywhere on [0, 4].

shortExplanation: The stem asks for the law of cosines, so use it to find the angle between the two equal sides, then apply Area = (1/2)*a*b*sin(C). This gives 12.
solutionSteps: Name the sides: the two equal sides are a = 5 and b = 5, and the side opposite the top angle C is c = 6.
Law of cosines: c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab*cos(C). Plug in: 36 = 25 + 25 - 2*5*5*cos(C), so 36 = 50 - 50*cos(C).
Solve for cos(C): 50*cos(C) = 50 - 36 = 14, so cos(C) = 14/50 = 0.28.
Find sin(C) using sin^2 + cos^2 = 1: sin(C) = sqrt(1 - 0.28^2) = sqrt(1 - 0.0784) = sqrt(0.9216) = 0.96.
Area of a triangle from two sides and the included angle: Area = (1/2)*a*b*sin(C) = (1/2)*5*5*0.96 = 12.5*0.96 = 12.
Quick sanity check: an isosceles triangle with base 6 has height sqrt(5^2 - 3^2) = 4, so area = (1/2)*6*4 = 12. Same answer, so we are safe.
keyConcept: Once you know two sides and the angle between them, the area is (1/2)*a*b*sin(C). The law of cosines is the tool that hands you that angle when you only know the three side lengths.
commonMistake: Multiplying side lengths together or forgetting the 1/2, which inflates the answer. Also, using cos(C) directly in the area formula instead of first converting it to sin(C).

optionExplanations.0: 10 is too small. It would need sin(C) = 0.8, but the actual sine here is 0.96.
optionExplanations.2: 15 is too large. The most a 5-by-5 pair can enclose is (1/2)*5*5 = 12.5 (a right angle), so 15 is impossible for these sides.
optionExplanations.3: 18 is far above the maximum possible area of 12.5 for two sides of length 5; it cannot happen.
optionExplanations.4: 20 is likewise impossible; it exceeds the largest area two sides of 5 could ever make.

formulaNotes: Law of cosines: c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab*cos(C). Area from two sides and included angle: Area = (1/2)*a*b*sin(C).

shortExplanation: sin θ + cos θ = sqrt(2)*sin(θ + 45), which equals sqrt(2) only when sin(θ + 45) = 1, i.e. θ + 45 = 90, so θ = 45 degrees.
solutionSteps: Rewrite sin θ + cos θ = sqrt(2) * sin(θ + 45).
Set sqrt(2) * sin(θ + 45) = sqrt(2), so sin(θ + 45) = 1.
Thus θ + 45 = 90, giving θ = 45 degrees.
Check: sin 45 + cos 45 = sqrt(2)/2 + sqrt(2)/2 = sqrt(2).
keyConcept: sin θ + cos θ = sqrt(2) * sin(θ + 45), whose maximum value sqrt(2) occurs at θ = 45.
commonMistake: Guessing 30 or 60 without recognizing that the sum peaks at sqrt(2) only at 45 degrees.

optionExplanations.0: 30 degrees gives 1/2 + sqrt(3)/2, which is less than sqrt(2).
optionExplanations.2: 60 degrees gives sqrt(3)/2 + 1/2, also less than sqrt(2).
optionExplanations.3: 75 degrees gives a value below sqrt(2) since it is past the peak at 45.

formulaNotes: sin θ + cos θ = sqrt(2) * sin(θ + 45).

shortExplanation: Every point satisfies y = 2x exactly, so the data lie on a perfect increasing straight line and the correlation coefficient is 1.
solutionSteps: Check the relationship: 2=2*1, 4=2*2, 6=2*3, 8=2*4, so y = 2x for all points.
A perfect linear relationship with positive slope gives correlation r = +1.
No scatter around the line means |r| is maximal.
keyConcept: A perfect positive linear relationship (y = a*x + b, a>0) yields correlation coefficient exactly +1.
commonMistake: Confusing the slope of the line with the correlation coefficient; r measures fit quality, not steepness.

optionExplanations.0: 0.5 would indicate only moderate linear association, but the fit here is perfect.
optionExplanations.1: 0.75 suggests noticeable scatter, which these exactly collinear points do not have.
optionExplanations.4: 0.9 is close but still implies imperfect alignment, whereas every point sits exactly on y=2x.

formulaNotes: For points lying exactly on y = a*x + b with a>0, r = +1 regardless of the value of a.

shortExplanation: A sphere inscribed in a cylinder touches the curved wall all around, so its radius equals the cylinder's radius, 3 cm.
solutionSteps: An inscribed sphere touches the lateral surface of the cylinder.
The sphere's great circle coincides with the cylinder's cross-section circle.
Therefore sphere radius = cylinder radius = 3 cm.
keyConcept: A sphere inscribed in a cylinder has the same radius as the cylinder (and diameter equal to the cylinder's height).
commonMistake: Adding to or scaling the radius; inscription means equality, not a larger value.

optionExplanations.1: 4 cm exceeds the cylinder radius, so the sphere would poke through the wall.
optionExplanations.2: 5 cm is even larger and impossible inside a radius-3 cylinder.
optionExplanations.3: 6 cm equals the cylinder's diameter, not its radius.

shortExplanation: The cube's space diagonal is s*sqrt(3); setting this to 2*sqrt(3) gives s=2, so the surface area is 6*2^2 = 24 cm^2.
solutionSteps: Space diagonal of a cube with edge s is s*sqrt(3).
Set s*sqrt(3) = 2*sqrt(3), giving s = 2 cm.
Surface area = 6*s^2 = 6*4 = 24 cm^2.
keyConcept: Cube space diagonal = edge*sqrt(3); surface area = 6*edge^2.
commonMistake: Using the face diagonal (s*sqrt(2)) instead of the space diagonal (s*sqrt(3)).

optionExplanations.1: 36 cm^2 corresponds to edge sqrt(6), which does not match diagonal 2*sqrt(3).
optionExplanations.2: 48 cm^2 corresponds to edge sqrt(8), giving a diagonal of 2*sqrt(6), not 2*sqrt(3).
optionExplanations.3: 72 cm^2 corresponds to edge sqrt(12)=2*sqrt(3), which would be the diagonal length, not the edge.

shortExplanation: Substituting y = 4 - x gives x^2 - x + (4 - k) = 0; a single solution requires the discriminant to be zero, yielding k = 3.75.
solutionSteps: From x + y = 4, write y = 4 - x.
Substitute into x^2 + y = k: x^2 + 4 - x = k, i.e. x^2 - x + (4 - k) = 0.
One solution means discriminant = 0: 1 - 4(4 - k) = 0.
keyConcept: A quadratic has exactly one (double) real root when its discriminant b^2 - 4ac equals zero.
commonMistake: Forgetting to substitute and instead guessing; the tangency condition comes from the discriminant.

optionExplanations.0: k = 3 gives discriminant 1 - 4(1) = -3 < 0, so no real solution.
optionExplanations.2: k = 12 gives discriminant 1 - 4(-8) = 33 > 0, producing two solutions.
optionExplanations.3: k = 14 gives a positive discriminant and thus two solutions, not one.

formulaNotes: Discriminant = 0 for a double root: 1 - 4(4 - k) = 0 -> k = 15/4.

shortExplanation: Adding a constant shifts all values equally and does not change the spread, so the standard deviation stays that of {2,4,6,8,10}, which is sqrt(8) ~ 2.83.
solutionSteps: Squared deviations: 16,4,0,4,16 summing to 40.
Population variance = 40/5 = 8, so standard deviation = sqrt(8) ~ 2.83.
Adding 5 to each value leaves deviations unchanged, so the standard deviation is unchanged.
keyConcept: Adding a constant to every data point leaves the standard deviation unchanged (it is translation-invariant).
commonMistake: Thinking the added constant increases the spread; only scaling (multiplication) affects standard deviation.

optionExplanations.0: 2.5 does not match the computed sqrt(8).
optionExplanations.2: 3 would be the value only if we ignored the invariance or miscounted deviations.
optionExplanations.4: 4 overstates the spread of this evenly-spaced set.

formulaNotes: sigma = sqrt( sum((x - mean)^2) / n ) = sqrt(40/5) = sqrt(8) ~ 2.83; adding a constant does not change sigma.

shortExplanation: Surface area of a box is 2(lw + lh + wh) = 2(35 + 45 + 63) = 286 cm^2.
solutionSteps: Compute the three distinct face areas: 5*7 = 35, 5*9 = 45, 7*9 = 63.
Double for the paired faces: 2*143 = 286 cm^2.
keyConcept: Rectangular box surface area = 2(lw + lh + wh).
commonMistake: Forgetting to double the sum of the three unique face areas.

optionExplanations.0: 214 cm^2 comes from an arithmetic slip in the face sums.
optionExplanations.1: 226 cm^2 does not match 2*143.
optionExplanations.2: 238 cm^2 does not match the correct total of 286.

shortExplanation: The center is at (0,3) and the point (0,6) is 3 units away, matching the distance 3 to the tangent x-axis, so the radius is 3 cm.
solutionSteps: Distance from center (0,3) to the x-axis is 3, which must equal the radius for tangency.
Distance from center (0,3) to (0,6) is |6 - 3| = 3.
Both give radius = 3 cm, consistently.
keyConcept: A circle tangent to a line has radius equal to the perpendicular distance from its center to that line.
commonMistake: Using the point (0,6) as if it were the center or doubling the distance to get a diameter.

optionExplanations.1: 4 cm would place the circle crossing the x-axis rather than tangent to it.
optionExplanations.2: 5 cm does not match either the tangency distance or the point distance.
optionExplanations.3: 6 cm is the y-coordinate of the given point, not the radius.

shortExplanation: Combined rate is 1/8 + 1/12 = 5/24 job per hour, so the time is 24/5 = 4.8 hours = 4 hours 48 minutes.
solutionSteps: John's rate = 1/8 job/hour; Mary's rate = 1/12 job/hour.
Combined rate = 1/8 + 1/12 = 3/24 + 2/24 = 5/24 job/hour.
0.8 hour = 48 minutes, so 4 hours 48 minutes.
keyConcept: Work rates add: combined time = 1 / (sum of individual rates).
commonMistake: Averaging the two times (getting 10 hours) instead of adding the rates.

optionExplanations.1: 5 hours slightly overstates the result of 4.8 hours.
optionExplanations.2: 6 hours ignores that two workers finish faster than either alone in relation to the rate sum.
optionExplanations.4: 4 hours is faster than the correct combined time of 4.8 hours.

shortExplanation: By the angle bisector theorem, AD bisects angle A exactly when it divides the opposite side in the ratio of the adjacent sides: AB/AC = BD/DC.
solutionSteps: The angle bisector from A meets BC at a point dividing BC proportionally to the adjacent sides.
That proportion is AB/AC = BD/DC.
So this ratio condition is the required characterization.
keyConcept: Angle bisector theorem: the bisector from a vertex splits the opposite side in the ratio of the two adjacent sides.
commonMistake: Assuming the bisector is also the median (BD = DC), which holds only for an isosceles triangle.

optionExplanations.0: BD = DC describes the median, true only when AB = AC.
optionExplanations.2: AD = BC is an unrelated length equality with no bearing on bisecting angle A.
optionExplanations.3: Angle B = Angle C makes the triangle isosceles but is not the general bisector condition.

shortExplanation: Building each term as the sum of the two before, starting 1, 3, gives 1,3,4,7,11,18,29; the seventh term is 29.
solutionSteps: Terms 1 and 2 are 1 and 3.
keyConcept: A Fibonacci-type recurrence: each term equals the sum of the two immediately preceding terms.
commonMistake: Miscounting the term index or restarting the addition from the wrong pair.

optionExplanations.0: 15 does not appear in the correctly generated sequence.
optionExplanations.1: 18 is the sixth term, not the seventh.
optionExplanations.2: 24 is not any term of this sequence.

shortExplanation: The first digit has 10 choices and each following digit has 9 (any digit except the one just before it), giving 10*9*9*9 = 7290.
solutionSteps: First digit: 10 possibilities (0-9).
Each subsequent digit must differ only from its immediate predecessor: 9 choices each.
keyConcept: For 'no two consecutive equal', each position after the first has (base - 1) choices relative to the previous one.
commonMistake: Requiring all digits distinct (10*9*8*7) instead of only forbidding equal neighbors.

optionExplanations.0: 5040 = 10*9*8*7 counts all-distinct codes, a stricter condition.
optionExplanations.1: 6561 = 9^4 wrongly restricts the first digit to 9 choices.
optionExplanations.3: 10000 = 10^4 ignores the no-consecutive-equal restriction entirely.

shortExplanation: Each pair of teams plays once, so matches = n(n-1)/2 = 45; solving gives n = 10.
solutionSteps: Number of matches in a round-robin is C(n,2) = n(n-1)/2.
keyConcept: A single round-robin among n teams has C(n,2) = n(n-1)/2 matches.
commonMistake: Using n(n-1) (counting each match twice) or n^2 instead of the combination.

optionExplanations.0: 9 teams give 9*8/2 = 36 matches, too few.
optionExplanations.2: 8 teams give 8*7/2 = 28 matches.
optionExplanations.3: 7 teams give 7*6/2 = 21 matches.

shortExplanation: In the worst case you draw all of the two largest groups (8 black + 5 red = 13) before any blue, so 14 pencils guarantee one of each color.
solutionSteps: To force all three colors, consider the worst case that delays the least common color.
The two largest counts are black (8) and red (5), totaling 13 pencils with only two colors.
One more pencil must be blue, so 13 + 1 = 14 guarantees one of each color.
